title: Delivery handoff: talk to resident on foot to complete delivery
Terrain: seeded low-poly island heightmap
Low-poly hover car model
description:
Faceted low-poly hover car: wedge hull, canopy, fin, hover pods/skirts, hard textures with flat colour panels. Built in code or from an asset file, using vertex colours plus one or two textures.

## Design
Static, hand-authored vertex data in src/car_mesh.c (fixed-function friendly — no VBOs):

- Wedge hull: front low, rear high, 8-10 silhouette verts. Do NOT share verts across facets — duplicated verts per facet give hard edges and flat normals (the PS1 look).
- Canopy: separate small wedge, dark glass color (~0.10, 0.12, 0.16), slightly inset.
- Rear fin + two side hover pods/skirt plates (flat quads, grey/white panels).
- Per-vertex colors: hull red (~0.85, 0.15, 0.10), trim white, glass dark — matches reference image 1/2 (red car-boat hybrid, low wedge profile, dark windshield).
- Optional single 32x32 hard-edged texture for hull via glTexCoordPointer; vertex colors remain primary.

API:

    void car_mesh_init(void);   // builds interleaved arrays {pos3, normal3, color3}
    void car_draw(void);        // glVertexPointer/glNormalPointer/glColorPointer + glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES)

Local origin: hull center on the contact plane, +Z forward, 1 unit = 1 m. Size: ~2.2 m long, 1.6 m wide, 1.1 m tall, skirt bottom at y=0.35 (hover clearance — the bob in island1-9gio moves the whole mesh).

## Done when
Silhouette matches the references (low wedge, dark windshield, red); every facet catches GL_LIGHT0 as a distinct flat plane (no smooth-shading seams); visible at 30 m through fog.

title: Water wake and delivery effects
description: Water spray particles behind the car, a fading trail on the ocean, and delivery pop effects (sparkles / floating text). Alpha-blended, pooled, fixed-function blending only.

title: island — hover-car package delivery game (PS1-style fixed-function)
description:
Recreate a PS1-style low-poly game: deliver packages to island inhabitants with a floating car that skates above water. OpenGL 1.2/1.5 fixed-function pipeline (GLAD gl=2.1 compat + GLFW legacy context, meson).

Decided: chase camera, car-like handling with drift, sandbox first (no timer in v1).
Target feel: low-poly faceted geometry, hard-edged low-res textures, NEAREST filtering, heavy distance fog, vertex jitter.

NOTE: reference screenshots could not be read by the agent (no image input), so art direction is provisional. Task A2 exists to capture a written spec from them before content work starts.

title: Delivery loop state machine
description:
Sandbox loop with no timer: idle free-roam, pickup package, deliver to the marked resident, award a small score/floating text, then pick a new random recipient. Driving back to the depot is always allowed.

## Design
src/delivery.c/h, stepped on the 60Hz tick (island1-mmap):

    typedef enum { DL_IDLE, DL_CARRYING, DL_DELIVERING } DeliveryPhase;

    typedef struct {
        DeliveryPhase phase;
        int  target_house;     // index into buildings[]
        uint32_t delivered;    // running score
        float deliver_timer;   // DL_DELIVERING countdown
    } DeliveryState;

Transitions:

    DL_IDLE:      near depot (dist < 4 m) AND package available AND input_pressed(ACT_PICKUP)
                  -> spawn parcel on car, pick target house (seeded RNG, reject within 40 m of car), spawn beacon (island1-p3qz), phase = DL_CARRYING
    DL_CARRYING:  dist(car, doorway(target)) < 3.0 AND input_pressed(ACT_DELIVER)
                  -> phase = DL_DELIVERING, deliver_timer = 0.6
    DL_DELIVERING: timer -= dt; at 0 -> delivered++, floating "+1" via island1-5stj,
                  phase = DL_IDLE, parcel despawned; re-pickup at depot allowed immediately

No timer/timeout anywhere — sandbox. Random pick uses the same PRNG family as island1-39q6 for determinism.

Expose for the HUD (island1-n7to): phase, target house id, delivered count; HUD strings: "GO TO DEPOT" / "DELIVER TO HOUSE N" / "DELIVERING...".

## Done when
Full loop pickup -> drive -> deliver -> "+1" -> beacon moves to a new house works end-to-end; re-pickup after delivery is possible; state never dead-ends (IDLE with no package but depot reachable is always valid).

Ocean plane with scrolling water texture
description:
Large ocean plane at sea level: scrolling hard-edged water texture with NEAREST sampling, two-layer offset for motion, colour grading toward the horizon and matching fog colour so the plane edge is invisible. Buoyant hover behaviour here is what makes the car read as floating.

## Design
- 300x300 unit quad centered on origin, y = SEA_LEVEL (0.0). Drawn before terrain; depth test on, no blending.
- Texture: hard-edged 64x64 water tile from island1-802h, GL_RGBA, GL_NEAREST, no mipmaps (mip shimmer kills the era look).
- Motion: the GL 1.2/1.5 compat context has NO multi-texture, so the "two-layer offset" becomes one trick: scroll the single layer in world space and tie the rate to the car's velocity — classic PS1 water.

    // world-space scroll, applied to the 4 quad's texture coords
    vec2 s = { car.pos[0] * 0.02f + t * 0.06f, car.pos[2] * 0.02f };
    texcoord = worldcoord * 0.5f + s;      // mod 1.0 in the vertex

  Net effect: water crawls when idle, rushes backwards at speed — no UV animation needed in a shader.
- Color: deep blue-green base (~0.05, 0.32, 0.38) via vertex colors, brighter toward center; the horizon seam disappears because fog color == sky color and fog END lands before the plane edge (see island1-a440).
- Foam/spray from wake is separate (island1-5stj) and renders after this pass.

## Done when
Scrolling freezes when the car stops; no visible plane edge from any camera height or angle; no mip shimmer when the car bobs.

title: Dev loop: git init, gitignore, run script
description: git init the repo, add .gitignore covering build/ build_macos/ subprojects/packagecache/, add a ./run.sh that sets up+compiles and execs the binary, document the meson commands in README. Commit the existing fixed-function scaffold as the baseline.

title: Render pass system with fixed-function state management
description:
Render passes built on a small state manager: sky/ocean/terrain/props/vehicle/particles/HUD, each with explicit lighting + fog + texture + blend state set on entry. Removes ad-hoc glEnable/glDisable scattered through draw code.

## Design
src/gfx.c/h — renderer tracks a GfxState and diffs against desired on each pass entry:

    typedef struct {
        uint32_t lighting :1, fog :1, texture :1, blend :1, depth_write :1;
        int      cull;            // GL_FRONT_AND_BACK / GL_NONE
        int      filter;          // GL_NEAREST / GL_LINEAR
        float    fog_start, fog_end;
        float    fog_color[4];
    } GfxState;

    void gfx_init(void);             // global defaults: LIGHT0/LIGHT1, cull, depth, NEAREST
    void gfx_set(const GfxState* d); // applies only the delta
    void gfx_push(void); void gfx_pop(void);  // save/restore (GL state is cheap to snapshot by re-apply)

Passes (src/passes.c, one function each, drawn in order):

    pass_sky, pass_ocean, pass_terrain, pass_props, pass_buildings,
    pass_vehicle, pass_particles, pass_beacon, pass_hud

- Moves the glEnable(GL_LIGHTING)/glDisable pairs currently in render_ground/render_axes (src/render.c:89,125,131,133) into their pass functions; render_init() becomes gfx_init().
- Beacon and HUD pass use push/pop so their blend/depth/lighting state never leaks into the next frame's sky pass.
- Fog color must equal sky color (see island1-a440) so the fog edge is invisible.

## Done when
No glEnable/glDisable remains outside gfx.c; commenting out any single pass leaves the rest rendering identically (no state bleed).

title: Collision: terrain height and prop colliders
description: World collision: sample terrain height for ground/air state, circle-vs-circle against prop and building colliders with a bounce/scrub response, keep the car on the ocean plane when over water.

title: Frame loop: fixed-timestep accumulator
Prop scatter system (rocks, palms, clutter)
description: Deterministic scatter of rocks, palms, crates, lamps, fences across island surfaces using a seeded PRNG and terrain slope/height rules. Each prop is low-poly with hard textures; returns a list of colliders for the vehicle.

title: HUD: package status, compass, speed
description: Orthographic overlay pass: package indicator, carried-parcel state, delivered count, speed readout, and a compass/minimap pointing at the active beacon. Rendered after the world with lighting off and depth writes disabled.

title: Shoreline and beach transition
description: Beach ring where terrain crosses sea level: sand blend, wet-sand darkening near the waterline, gentle foam line drawn as geometry or texture band. Visual anchor that reads the island edge.

title: Delivery target beacon
description: Prominent PS1-style beacon at the active recipient's doorway: translucent column or floating holo marker visible above terrain, scaled/alpha-faded with distance so it reads from across the island.

title: Package pickup entity and carry state
description: Spawn a package at a delivery depot on the island; carrying it attaches a parcel mesh to the car and switches HUD state. Picking up again is possible after delivery.

title: Camera collision and above-terrain clamping
description: Raise the chase camera when terrain intrudes between camera and car; clamp camera above terrain/water height so it never clips through the island or dips under the ocean plane.

title: NPC inhabitants with idle and delivery reaction
description: Low-poly island inhabitants near buildings: blocky humanoid, idle sway, turns to face the player, reaction on delivery. Palette-locked flat colours, no skeletal animation needed.

title: Write art-direction spec from reference screenshots
description: The agent cannot read the reference screenshots. Someone must transcribe them into a written art spec: palette (sky/ocean/grass/sand hex values), camera framing and FOV, texture resolution and filtering, fog color/density, silhouette language of car/islands/buildings/NPCs, HUD layout. This spec is the contract for all content tasks (terrain, ocean, car, buildings, textures).

comments.author: hayden
comments.text:
## Reference Image 1 — transcription (provided by user)

Overall: distinctive **PS1-era low-poly retro aesthetic**.

**Foreground & Water**
- Lower half of frame: body of water on textured, low-poly polygonal planes; subtle horizontal ripples; deep blue-green gradients.
- Left side: sharp, blocky splash of white foam erupting from the water surface.

**Vehicle**
- Low-poly red vehicle (retro car / speedboat hybrid) cruising across the water.
- Flat polygonal facets, dark windshield, low profile.

**Midground & Structures**
- Sloping low-poly grassy hill rises against the horizon, dotted with blocky pixelated green trees.
- Near water's edge: rustic wooden dock/structure with small industrial elements — a vertical post and a small tank.

**Background & Sky**
- Bright vibrant blue sky; large stylized chunky white cumulus clouds with blocky pixelated edges.
- Single prominent tree-topped green hill standing tall against the cloudscape.

**UI Overlays** (video-player chrome, likely not part of game art)
- Top corners: playback + audio icons (left); closed captions, options, full-screen icons (right).

Status: provisional art direction input for the spec. Hex palette values, camera FOV/framing, texture resolutions, fog params still TBD.

## Reference Image 2 — transcription (provided by user)

Continues the same **PS1 low-poly retro aesthetic**.

**Foreground & Water Action**
- Camera angle shifts closer to the water's surface.
- Same low-poly red vehicle carving aggressively through choppy blue-green water.
- Large jagged wake of sharp white water plumes and spray erupting directly behind the vehicle — dramatic sense of speed.

**Vehicle**
- Low-poly red car-boat hybrid angled sharply (banking/turning).
- Angular faceted body panels, low wedge profile, dark windshield texture.

**UI Overlays**

**Background**
- Upper distance: low-poly island with sloping green terrain, blocky pixelated trees, and a small rustic structure near the coast.
- Bright clear blue sky with a small wispy cloud at the very top.
